name: GitHub
description: Repositories, branches, pull requests, issues, and Actions.
auth_note: Use a fine-grained personal access token as the bearer token.

name: Linear
auth_note: Linear's remote MCP server uses OAuth sign-in, which Jhin does not support yet. Use the native Linear app with a personal API key instead.

name: Vercel
auth_note: The remote server uses OAuth; the native Vercel app works with an access token.

name: Supabase
description: Projects, database queries, edge functions, and logs.
auth_note: The hosted server signs in with OAuth; the native Supabase app uses a management token or database connection.

name: Notion
description: Pages, databases, and comments in your Notion workspace.
auth_note: Notion's hosted server uses OAuth sign-in (not supported yet). Self-host the open-source Notion MCP server with an integration token as a bearer token instead.

name: Slack
auth_note: Slack has no official hosted MCP server; run a community server with a bot token and enter its URL.
setup_note: Self-host a Slack MCP server (for example the reference server from the MCP community) behind HTTPS and paste its URL.

name: Atlassian (Jira & Confluence)
description: Jira issues and Confluence pages through Atlassian's remote server.
auth_note: Atlassian's remote server uses OAuth sign-in, which Jhin does not support yet; self-hosted servers with API tokens work with the bearer option.

name: Stripe
auth_note: Use a restricted API key as the bearer token.

name: HubSpot
auth_note: HubSpot's remote server uses OAuth; check the docs for the current endpoint.

name: Sentry
auth_note: The hosted server uses OAuth; self-host sentry-mcp with an auth token for the bearer option.

name: Cloudflare
description: Cloudflare documentation search (no sign-in). Other Cloudflare servers need OAuth.

name: PayPal
auth_note: Use an access token from PayPal's developer dashboard.

name: Zapier MCP
description: Thousands of apps through your personal Zapier MCP server.
auth_note: Your Zapier MCP URL is personal and already authenticates you; keep it private.
setup_note: Create a server at zapier.com/mcp, copy its unique URL, and paste it here.

name: Asana
auth_note: Asana's remote server uses OAuth sign-in (not supported yet).

name: ClickUp
setup_note: Self-host a ClickUp MCP server with an API token and paste its URL.

name: Canva
auth_note: Canva's server uses OAuth sign-in (not supported yet).

name: Figma
auth_note: Figma's remote server uses OAuth sign-in (not supported yet).

name: Google Drive
setup_note: Google does not host a Drive MCP server; self-host a community server configured with your Google credentials.

name: Google Calendar
setup_note: Self-host a community Google Calendar MCP server and paste its URL.

name: Gmail
setup_note: Self-host a community Gmail MCP server and paste its URL.

name: Airtable
setup_note: Community server; run it behind HTTPS and paste its URL.

name: PostgreSQL
description: Read-only SQL over a Postgres database.
setup_note: Needs a self-hosted MCP server; stdio servers are not supported yet. For Supabase databases use the native Supabase app.

name: Playwright browser
description: Drive a real browser: navigate, click, read pages.
setup_note: Run playwright-mcp with --port behind HTTPS and paste its URL. Only connect servers you trust: browsing tools can reach any site.

name: Filesystem
description: Read and write files in allowed directories.
setup_note: Needs a self-hosted MCP server; stdio is not supported yet. For isolated file work use the CLI sandbox app.

name: Brave Search
setup_note: Self-host the Brave Search MCP server with your API key and paste its URL.

name: Tavily
description: Search, extract, and crawl the web.
auth_note: Tavily's hosted endpoint expects the API key in the URL, which Jhin does not store; check the docs for header-based auth or self-host.

name: Exa
description: Neural web search and content retrieval.
auth_note: Check the docs for how the API key is passed; URL query keys are not supported.

name: Firecrawl
description: Scrape and crawl websites into clean text.
auth_note: Firecrawl's hosted endpoint embeds the API key in the URL; prefer self-hosting with a header token.

name: Context7
description: Up-to-date library documentation for coding agents.
auth_note: Works without a key; add an API key with the custom header option for higher limits.

name: Resend
setup_note: Self-host the Resend MCP server with your API key and paste its URL.

name: Twilio
setup_note: Self-host Twilio's MCP server with an API key and paste its URL.

name: Discord
setup_note: Self-host a community Discord MCP server with a bot token and paste its URL.

name: Telegram
description: Chats and messages through a bot.
setup_note: Self-host a community Telegram MCP server with a bot token and paste its URL.

name: Trello
setup_note: Self-host a community Trello MCP server with an API key and token, then paste its URL.

name: Dropbox
setup_note: Self-host a community Dropbox MCP server with an access token and paste its URL.

name: Hugging Face
auth_note: Works anonymously; add a Hugging Face token as the bearer token for private resources.

name: DeepWiki
description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository.

name: Microsoft Learn
description: Official Microsoft and Azure documentation search.

name: Neon
description: Serverless Postgres projects, branches, and SQL.
auth_note: Neon's remote server uses OAuth; self-host neon-mcp with an API key for the bearer option.

name: Any HTTP API
description: Generic HTTP requests against any API with a fixed base URL — bearer, custom-header, or basic auth.
auth_note: Pick the auth scheme the API expects when connecting; unauthenticated APIs work too.

name: Fake MCP (dev)
description: The dev stack's fake MCP server: echo, notes, a destructive tool, an image, and huge text.
auth_note: Dev-only. Bearer token: fake-mcp-token. In-network URL: http://fake-mcp:8080/mcp
setup_note: Only available with the dev compose overlay (service fake-mcp).
